trigger: an enrolled agent loops frames with a valid-shape registry-<hex> command_id, action set_value and 300 audit| lines of about 4 KiB each (about 1.2 MB of 365-day evidence per frame, no ceiling on the number of frames)
classification_rationale: no per-agent or per-time bound existed on agent-triggered audit writes, only per-frame bounds, although the repo already rules the class a defect (the OTA identity limiter comment in agent_service_impl.cpp, bounded_audit_budget.hpp, observability-conventions.md); I5 raised to HIGH by unbounded, persistent growth on the path that carries audit evidence and shares the Postgres pool with auth and RBAC; security-guardian labelled it MEDIUM and compliance-officer HIGH, the derived band governs
summary: One enrolled agent could loop frames with a valid-shape registry command id, a mutating action and 300 audit| lines, writing about 300 synchronous audit rows (about 1.2 MB of 365-day evidence) per frame with no ceiling on frames, on the Postgres pool every store shares. Security-guardian and compliance-officer found it independently; the design had accepted per-frame bounds only. Fixed in 470e74049: every row is charged to a per-agent fixed-window budget (600 rows per 60 seconds), a refused row is counted (reason=suppressed) and never queued, and one summary line is logged per window. The re-review found two flaws in that first budget (rab-budget-key-first-96-bytes and rab-agent-table-sampling-cliff, both fixed in 577d75fe8); batching a frame into one transaction is deferred (rab-one-commit-per-row-no-batch-write).

policy_floor: ownership/lifetime defect enumerated by cpp-safety's blocking contract (borrowed-data escape: a raw pointer dereferenced on untracked, ambiguously-owned detached threads)
trigger: server stop() (SIGTERM) while a gateway-forwarded registry mutating frame with audit| lines is inside the hook on a detached forwarder thread
classification_rationale: process_gateway_response runs on the detached per-command forwarder threads that stop() does not drain; the hook dereferenced the plain audit_store_ there across up to 300 writes, a use-after-free window the base code did not have, and the repo gives every store newly reachable from those threads the weak-holder treatment; the Gate 1 resource ledger sentence 'for the duration of one call' omitted the reach. cpp-safety gates it by the lifetime policy floor (derived MEDIUM: I5, E5); the other four reviewers derived MEDIUM and recorded newly-reachable, cpp-safety recorded introduced (contested, so introduced)
summary: The new audit hook dereferenced the raw audit_store_ pointer on the detached forwarder threads that shutdown does not drain, while stop() nulls and frees the store: a use-after-free window the base code did not have, found independently by five reviewers and gated by the lifetime policy floor. Fixed in 470e74049 the way the analytics store was treated: the server owns the store as a shared_ptr, the service holds a weak_ptr written once at wiring and never cleared, the pure verdict runs first, and the store is locked per frame only when the frame owes rows or a flag. The re-review confirmed the hook no longer reads the raw pointer (ASan, UBSan and TSan probes); the residual, the pool the store borrows and the detached thread itself, is the pre-existing #3279 gap, unchanged. The first test evidence for the closure was weak (rab-closure-mechanisms-have-no-observing-test-or-gate).

trigger: std::bad_alloc inside the audit hook (about 2.5 MB per 300 x 4 KiB frame) on a Subscribe stream thread or a detached forwarder thread
classification_rationale: every sibling store call on agent data is firewalled (ReportInventory, the signer, try_persist_audit); the hook was the one without
summary: The hook was the only agent-data store call with no exception firewall: a throw ends a Subscribe stream with UNKNOWN and skips its cleanup, and on a detached forwarder thread it is std::terminate. Fixed in 470e74049: the hook is a member function wrapped in a try/catch that reports a throw as a failed write. The re-review found the try opened after the pure verdict and the store lock, so the comment promised more than the code covered; recorded as rab-hook-firewall-narrower-than-its-comment (fixed in 577d75fe8).

trigger: the audit INSERT failing fast (table unavailable, read-only primary after failover) while one stream keeps sending registry mutating frames
classification_rationale: signal_grpc_audit_failed had only one-shot callers; the first per-frame use appends to a multimap for the life of the call and the trailer is delivered only when the stream closes
summary: signal_grpc_audit_failed was called once per failed frame inside the Subscribe read loop, so the call's trailing-metadata multimap grew for the life of the stream and the trailer surfaced only at stream close. Found by cpp-safety, security-guardian and sre. Fixed in 470e74049: a local flag declared before the read loop (audit_failed_signalled) sets the trailer once per stream, and the lexical gate pins that the flag is declared once, before the loop, and that both Subscribe hooks use it.

trigger: a producer that replaces or escapes only | and echoes a registry key or value name holding LF or CR: an LF inside a field forges a second audit row with a chosen result, a trailing CR turns result=ok into ok_ (a failure row)
classification_rationale: the producer contract and the audit-log row named only the pipe, while the extractor splits on LF before the scrub and reads result from the line, so an LF or CR inside a field changes the rows; compliance-officer derived MEDIUM (I7, E3, probe-verified); security-guardian and architect derived LOW because no producer emits audit| lines yet (E6); the strongest derived band is recorded
summary: The producer contract (header banner and audit-log row) forbade only | inside a field. A probe showed an LF inside a field mints a second row whose result the endpoint chooses, and a CR flips result=ok to a failure; five reviewers raised it, agreeing the server half is verified and the producer is future. Fixed in 470e74049: the contract now requires no |, LF or CR inside a field, one record per LF-terminated line and result= before any caller-sized field (the registry plugin's own sanitize_field already strips all three). The re-review found the word 'escape' wrong for a backslash; recorded as rab-contract-says-escape-but-a-backslash-pipe-still-picks-the-result.

trigger: an audit| line over 4,096 bytes with result= late in the line (old= and new= are the trailing fields): the cut dropped result=ok, the row said failure, and nothing flagged, logged or marked the cut
classification_rationale: the audit-log row said the row records the line's own result=ok, while the code read result from the cut text; unhappy-path derived MEDIUM from I8 and E3 (the flat table gives LOW; the stronger recorded band is kept); the other four reviewers recorded LOW or INFO (visibly incomplete, bound documented, fail-safe direction)
summary: A line longer than 4,096 bytes was cut with no flag, log or marker, and result= was read from the cut text, so a true success whose result sat late in a long line was stored as a failure while the row read as a complete, shorter line. Fixed in 470e74049: result is read from the whole line before any cut, a cut line sets the frame's truncated flag (counted as reason=truncated and warned once per frame) and its row carries the server token cut=1 after agent=, and the documents say a long line loses its tail. A mutation run over the new tests killed the mutants that read the result from the cut text, dropped the marker and dropped the truncation count.

trigger: an auditor or agentic worker follows the documented join: target_type=Command&target_id=<command_id>
classification_rationale: new rows stored Command while command.dispatch and command.outbox_delivered store command, and the audit query matches target_type exactly, so the documented join returned this change's rows and never the dispatcher's; compliance-officer derived MEDIUM (I6); architect, docs-writer and consistency-auditor derived LOW (I8), consistency-auditor labelling it medium natively; the strongest derived band is recorded
summary: registry.write rows stored target_type Command while the dispatch rows they join to store command, and the audit query matches the type exactly, so the join the audit-log row documents found the endpoint's row and never the operator's. Found by four reviewers. Fixed in 470e74049: the row stores command, the tests pin it (a mutation back to Command fails the suite), and the audit-log table's spelling for command.dispatch is corrected.

trigger: a customer or auditor reads the SOC 2 inventory row and the audit-log row as the statement of who can read the registry.write rows and what the evidence is
classification_rationale: the row omitted that the rows are endpoint-asserted, pointed at an erasure path the cited rows do not give (TTL only), named secrets but not the personal data the rows carry (SIDs, paths, values), listed the legacy /events stream without saying any authenticated non-service-scoped session can open it, left Administrator out of the reader list, and said nothing is persisted on the endpoint although the plugin logs HKLM Run and Services key paths; security-guardian and consistency-auditor recorded LOW and INFO for the reader-list parts, the strongest band is recorded
summary: The SOC 2 inventory row for registry.write understated the evidence's limits: it did not say the rows are asserted by the endpoint, pointed at an erasure path that is TTL-only, named secrets but not the personal data the rows carry, listed the readers incompletely (Administrator; the legacy /events stream open to any authenticated non-service-scoped session), and said nothing is persisted on the endpoint although the plugin logs key paths. Fixed in 470e74049 with one clause for each point. The re-review checked every claim in the row against the role seeds, the topology floor and the /events gate and found them accurate.

trigger: a gateway-connected agent runs a registry mutation that finishes more than 300 s after dispatch (delay plus stagger plus run time; /api/command accepts delay and stagger up to 300 s each)
classification_rationale: the transport loss is pre-existing and the loss class was disclosed ('a stream that drops'), but this trigger and its outcome (mutation applied, no row, execution resolves FAILURE or stays unresolved) were not; the omission is introduced
summary: The gateway's SendCommand window is fixed at 300 s and later frames are dropped as orphans, so a gateway-connected agent whose command finishes after delay, stagger and run time exceed 300 s applies the mutation and mints no row, while the audit-log row named only 'a stream that drops'. Fixed in 470e74049 by stating the window and its outcome in the audit-log row and the SOC 2 row. Widening the window to cover delay and stagger is a gateway transport change carried with the emitting plugin change; rab-chaos-scenarios holds the boundary scenario.

trigger: a registry mutating frame with a non-minted command_id, more than 300 audit| lines, or an INSERT failing mid-frame: a lost row was knowable only from a WARN
classification_rationale: the repo's convention is a metric as the signal and the audit row as the evidence; the existing emit-failed counter moves once per frame, not per lost row, and the other loss paths had no counter at all
summary: Three evidence-loss paths (a frame ignored for an unmintable id, lines past the cap, rows after a failed INSERT) were visible only in a WARN, and the existing emit-failed counter moves once per frame, not per lost row. Fixed in 470e74049 with one counter family, yuzu_server_registry_audit_dropped_total{reason}, described and pre-seeded in server.cpp and documented in metrics.md: suppressed and persist_failed count rows, unmintable_id and truncated count frames. No new alert ships, deliberately (see rab-cost-is-rows-not-bytes-and-no-alert-on-the-new-counters). The re-review found the documents call the counter complete, which it is not; recorded as rab-counter-described-as-complete-but-is-not.

trigger: a later gateway or proto edit drops or defaults field 8 on a non-Guardian response frame while the Erlang suite stays green
classification_rationale: gateway-mode registry.write rows depend on CommandResponse.action surviving the gateway for the first time; mutations that dropped the field at either hop (yuzu_gw_agent.erl:430, yuzu_gw_mgmt_service.erl:283) left all five relevant existing modules green; gateway mode is non-default (E4)
summary: Nothing in the Erlang suite pinned CommandResponse.action (field 8) across the gateway's ordinary response hops, although gateway-mode audit rows depend on it for the first time; mutations that dropped the field at either hop left every existing test green. Fixed in 470e74049 with two eunit tests, one in yuzu_gw_agent_tests.erl (the forwarded frame keeps action, RUNNING and terminal) and one in yuzu_gw_mgmt_service_tests.erl (the SendCommandResponse re-encode); a mutation run showed each mutant turning exactly one test red. The re-review found the encode-side pin checked the key, not the field number (rab-erlang-wire-pin-checks-the-key-not-the-field-number).

trigger: a one-token edit to the result rule: '|result=' to 'result=', '== ok' to starts_with('ok'), or accepting OK
classification_rationale: the file's eight pure cases were built standalone against one-token header edits and these survived; the live cases use only registry-<alnum> ids and fixed line shapes, so they cannot kill them; the header's claim that every rule is pinned was false
summary: Mutation probing of the extractor's pure cases left survivors in the result rule: replacing the |result= delimiter, loosening == ok to a prefix test and accepting OK all stayed green, and a refused write whose key held result=ok could then be recorded as success. Fixed in 470e74049 with cases for a result= inside an earlier field, result=okay and result=OK (all failure) and a corrected header claim; a later mutation run over the fixed tests killed the delimiter and prefix mutants at the intended assertions.

trigger: a frame whose command_id is registry, registry-, Registry-9, registry-ext-<hex> or registry-zzz with a mutating action stamped by the agent
classification_rationale: the header said only registry-<16|32 hex> ids exist and the function name is_server_minted_command_id claimed more than it checked; a valid shape stays forgeable by an endpoint (declared)
summary: The id check accepted any identifier of 1 to 160 characters from a wide charset, so ids the server never mints (registry, registry-, registry-zzz) minted rows and the function name claimed more than it checked. Fixed in 470e74049: the check is the exact shape the server mints, registry- (the plugin spelling compared ASCII-case-insensitively) plus 16 or 32 lowercase hex digits; the 160-byte cap and its derivation are gone and the tests use hex ids. A valid shape stays forgeable by an endpoint and is documented as agent-asserted. The re-review verified the predicate with a 26-case probe; the gaps in its test table are recorded as rab-exact-id-predicate-test-holes.

trigger: a reader stops at the release-note lead, the conventions bullet or the header comment: the server path is live on deploy but the text reads as dormant, and the header says the plugin guarantees a property no plugin yet provides
classification_rationale: the required audit-action row exists and already says the rows are agent-asserted, so no document is missing (I9, not I7); the gap is that the customer text left out a consequence of the accepted design
summary: The audit-log and SOC 2 rows opened 'Dormant ... no rows are written', true of shipped agents and plugins only: the server path is live on deploy for any enrolled agent, with bounds stated per frame and no per-agent limit. The changelog led with the capability and put dormancy last, the conventions bullet carried no dormant marker and the header said 'the plugin guarantees'. Fixed in 470e74049 with one sentence per row stating the server side is live on deploy, a dormancy lead on the changelog entry and a producer-must wording in the header. The re-review found the changelog still understated the live ingest; recorded as rab-changelog-understates-live-ingest-and-endpoint-assertion.

trigger: an SRE decides how to alert on a dropped registry.write row from the audit-log and conventions text
classification_rationale: the docs named only the trailer; the gRPC timing part (a trailer on a long-lived stream reaches the agent when the stream closes) is reasoned from gRPC semantics, not run, hence likely
summary: The documents described a failed audit write only as the audit-failed trailer, which by gRPC semantics reaches the agent when the stream closes and which nothing under agents/ reads, and never named the real-time signal: every failed write is logged and moves yuzu_server_audit_emit_failed_total, which the YuzuAuditPersistFailures alert watches. Fixed in 470e74049: the audit-log row and the conventions bullet name the log line, the metric and the alert, and say when the trailer is delivered.

trigger: an auditor or operator relies on 'never sees a mutation complete before its audit row exists' or on 'stored as emitted'
classification_rationale: the response-store row and the SSE publish both precede the hook, so the claim holds only for the tracker advance and the agent-transition event, and 'stored as emitted' contradicted the cut and the control-byte scrub; security-guardian derived LOW (I8), the other two INFO (I9), all map to NICE
summary: The executions-ladder subsection said an operator never sees a mutation complete before its audit row exists, but the response-store row and the SSE publish both precede the hook; only the tracker advance and the agent-transition event follow it. The conventions bullet's 'stored as emitted' contradicted the bounds and the control-byte scrub. Fixed in 470e74049: the ladder claim is scoped to the tracker advance and agent-transition, and the conventions bullet says 'as emitted apart from the bounds'.

trigger: a maintainer sizes the worst-case delay from a comment, or reads the hook comment as describing what the agent does with its terminal frame, or relies on 'every ordinary plugin-output frame' carrying the stamp
classification_rationale: each comment contradicts the code it sits beside (a truth finding owned by cpp-expert), none adjacent to an authorisation branch
summary: Comments contradicted the code in four places: a saturated pool costs up to the audit store's 4 s write timeout per INSERT, not about 500 ms; the hook comment described 'a plugin that returns its rows only at the end' although this agent flushes output as RUNNING frames and its terminal frame carries none; the header banner said the stamp rides on every ordinary output frame although timing and keepalive frames carry output and no action; and an agent member comment named the wrong source for the final frame's action. Fixed in 470e74049: each comment says what the code does, with the terminal hook described as defence in depth.

trigger: a reader follows a stale pointer or counts a byte in a comment
classification_rationale: the cite of agent_service_impl.hpp:113 was pre-existing but carried into new text; the rest was introduced by the move of the shared helper
summary: Stale pointers and a miscount: three places cited agent_service_impl.hpp:113 for the shutdown contract (it is set_execution_tracker's doc); test_runtime_config_helpers.hpp still named test_agent_service_impl.cpp as the TrackerScope home after the helper moved; a test header and the lexical gate's docstring misdescribed what the tests cover; and a test comment said 4091 ASCII bytes where the code builds 4089. Fixed in 470e74049 by citing the symbol and correcting each sentence.

trigger: a compliance remediation whose fix is registry.set_value, delete_value or delete_key: the policy evaluator dispatches as a system caller with a registry-<32 hex> command id, so rows are minted
classification_rationale: the change summary said internal system dispatches mint nothing because the plugin is not registry, but the guards key on the execution id, not the command id; the behaviour is newly reachable and the documentation gap is introduced; consistency-auditor labelled it medium natively and derived LOW, the derived band governs
summary: The change summary said internal system dispatches mint nothing because the plugin is not registry, but the guards key on the execution id, and the policy evaluator dispatches a registry mutating fix as a system caller with a registry-<32 hex> command id, which mints rows; the audit-log row named no operator row for them. Fixed in 470e74049: the audit-log row says a compliance remediation has no command-id-keyed operator row, and the summary note was corrected. The re-review found the new sentence itself contradicted the policy.remediate row; recorded as rab-operator-row-joins-misnamed-in-audit-log.

trigger: a later change adds a mutating registry action outside capability fragment a: it would run unaudited with every test green
classification_rationale: the test says it ties kRegistryMutatingActions to the catalogue but iterated one of 28 fragments (23 of 28 are per-plugin files); E6 today because no further mutating registry action exists
summary: The test that ties kRegistryMutatingActions to the capability catalogue iterated one of 28 fragments, so a mutating registry row added elsewhere would run unaudited while the test, which says it ties the two lists together, stayed green. Fixed in 470e74049: the cross-check iterates every capability fragment, as test_enablement_units.cpp does, and asserts the number of registry rows.

trigger: not applicable: a static convention (docs/cpp-conventions.md lists output parameters under 'Forbidden in new code')
classification_rationale: the conventions document has no waiver clause and the same header already had a result struct; not a policy floor, the clause sits in the routed document's reading list, not in a catastrophic row
summary: extract_registry_audit_lines filled a bool* output parameter, which docs/cpp-conventions.md forbids in new code, while the same header already had a result struct. Fixed in 470e74049: it returns a struct of lines and the truncated flag, with the per-line ok and cut flags computed from the uncut line.

trigger: a producer line of audit| plus 4,091 or more continuation bytes (0x80-0xBF, not valid UTF-8), total over 4,096 bytes
classification_rationale: the retreat cannot underflow or read out of bounds (the first six bytes are always audit|), but on this input only 'audit' survives and a row is still minted; agent-asserted data is accepted by design (E3); verified with an ASan and UBSan probe
summary: The UTF-8 back-off at the 4,096-byte cut retreated without a bound: on invalid input of audit| plus 4,091 or more continuation bytes it kept only 'audit', losing the separator and the body, yet still minted a row. There was no underflow or out-of-bounds read. Fixed in 470e74049: the retreat is bounded to three steps (a UTF-8 sequence is at most four bytes) and invalid input is cut at the bound; the re-review re-checked it under ASan and UBSan with 240 straddle cases, non-UTF-8 runs and 3,000 random frames.

trigger: an agent-transition published after the test body ends (none is possible today: the tracker and bus destructors are defaulted and have no thread)
classification_rationale: the exec_bus listener captured two locals by reference that were declared after the bus and so die first; it is a std::function owned by the bus, not an fd, handle or ABI callback, so no Resource Ledger floor. The reorder was planned for the first fix round but the locals were still declared after the bus at 470e74049, and cpp-safety found the same lines again at the re-review (cpp-safety native NICE, derived INFO, exposure E6)
summary: In the ordering test the exec-bus listener captured two locals declared after the bus, so they die first; nothing can publish after the body ends today. The reorder was planned for the first fix round but was not applied there, and cpp-safety found the same lines at the re-review. Fixed in 577d75fe8 by declaring the two locals above the bus.

trigger: a one-token edit: the UTF-8 'while' to 'if', dropping '_' or '.' from the id charset, or moving the A, Z or z range ends
classification_rationale: six header mutants survived the pure cases (the test straddled a two-byte character only; no test id held the charset members); E6 caps at LOW because ids are <registry>-<lowercase hex> and sanitize_pg_text repairs a split character at INSERT
summary: Six header mutants survived the pure cases: the multi-step UTF-8 walk-back (the test straddled a two-byte character only) and the id charset members (no test id held the underscore, the dot or the range ends). Fixed in 470e74049 with three- and four-byte characters straddling byte 4,096 and an id exercising the charset; the charset was then replaced by the exact hex shape (rab-command-id-check-admits-ids-the-server-never-mints), whose test-table holes are recorded as rab-exact-id-predicate-test-holes.

trigger: a later edit to the hook's clock argument, a failing row after earlier rows, or a log capture that cannot see the logger
classification_rationale: quality-engineer derived LOW; happy-path recorded LOW (I9, E3, verified) for the timestamp; the third item of the same quality-engineer finding, runtime ordering at the other three hook sites, is rejected separately (rab-runtime-ordering-proof-at-three-hooks)
summary: Three live-ingest gaps: every fault case failed at row 0, so 'earlier rows persist' and the count of rows not attempted were unpinned; the log-silence case asserted only the absence of a line, the negative-only shape a dead capture also satisfies; and no live case read the row's timestamp, which the store replaces with 'now' if it is not positive. Fixed in 470e74049: a CHECK-constraint fault fails the middle row of three (one row persists, emit_failed moves, '1 further row(s)' is logged), a positive log assertion sits beside the negative one, and the first live ingest is bracketed by two clock reads.

trigger: a reword of the gateway error log line
classification_rationale: the gate embedded the whole spdlog::error text, which the unit test already pins; a wording-only edit reports 'found 0' without the delta (probe-verified)
summary: The static wiring gate embedded the whole gateway spdlog::error text in its pattern, which the unit test already pins, so a wording-only edit reported 'expected exactly two gateway hooks (found 0)' without naming the change. Fixed in 470e74049: the gate matches the whole spdlog::error(...) statement by regular expression.

trigger: a later edit moves a Subscribe hook or the gateway terminal hook after notify_exec_tracker
classification_rationale: rejected, not deferred: a runtime proof at the other three sites needs a Subscribe-with-tracker harness that has no precedent in the tree, while the static lexical gate is the repo idiom (the gateway-peer registration gate) and a reorder is detected by it (nine of nine gate mutants were killed at the time of the ruling, and the self-test mutates the real sources); E6 for this item because the gate blocks a reorder
summary: Ordering of the hook before the tracker advance is proved at run time only at the gateway RUNNING site; the other three rest on the static gate. Not adopted: a runtime proof at the Subscribe sites and the gateway terminal site would need a harness that does not exist, while the lexical gate pins the site count, the order and the failure signal and fails on a reorder, as its in-file mutation self-test shows against the real sources. The executions-ladder subsection states that these sites have no runtime ordering test.

trigger: the audit store handed to the hook is non-null but closed
classification_rationale: rejected with code evidence at dd392181a: server.cpp:6264 wires the hook only when audit_store_ && is_open(), startup refuses to boot on a store that failed to open (server.cpp:5610), and AuditStore::open_ is write-once (audit_store.cpp:317), so a closed store is never wired; quality-engineer reached the same conclusion independently (coverage map: needs no test); derived INFO, native SHOULD for a missing failure-path test
summary: The early-out for a non-null but closed audit store had no test. Rejected: the hook is wired only for an open store, startup refuses to boot on a store that failed to open, and the open flag is write-once, so the branch cannot be reached in production; quality-engineer concluded independently that it needs no test.

trigger: an enrolled agent streaming 300-line frames: each row is its own lease, INSERT and commit on the stream thread before the tracker advances (about 16 such streams saturate the 16-connection pool every store shares)
classification_rationale: unhappy-path derived MEDIUM (I5, I8; provenance newly-reachable); sre and architect derived LOW (introduced; contested, so introduced). Not needed by the accepted scope and an independent surface: a new AuditStore API with its own rollback and metric semantics, which follows the rule that behaviour comes first and the optimisation is its own change; the per-agent budget bounds the rows batching would save
summary: Each audit row is written with its own lease, INSERT and commit, so a frame of up to 300 rows holds the stream thread (or a forwarder thread) for rows times commit latency ahead of the tracker advance, and a mid-frame failure leaves a persisted prefix; the budget bounds rows but not commits. The wording was corrected in 470e74049 (the delay is rows times commit latency, not the write timeout) and the budget limits the volume. Deferred: one transaction per frame through a new AuditStore::log_batch, with the admission loop already separated from the write; the owner files it after the change is raised.

trigger: an enrolled agent loops output frames with a mutating action and a non-minted command_id, or frames over a bound: each frame writes a WARN into the synchronous rotating log
classification_rationale: the counters are unsampled and complete for these frames, so the lines are an additional log-volume lever; a throttle changes the warn-once-per-frame tests and the gateway peer guard's keyed-budget precedent applies; raised a second time, independently, by a fresh sre run at the re-review of the fixes, and still deferred
summary: The warnings for a frame ignored for an unmintable id and for a frame that hit a bound are written per frame with no throttle, so a looping agent can fill the synchronous rotating log at wire speed; the counters already carry the complete signal, and the direct-path persist-failure line lacked the command id. The command id was added to that line in 470e74049. Deferred: gate the two warnings through a reason-keyed DenialAuditBudget as the gateway peer guard does; the owner files it after the change is raised.

trigger: an auditor investigates a registry.write row and needs the transport it arrived on: sibling agent audit rows carry source_ip and session_id, these rows do not
classification_rationale: the rows are endpoint-asserted, so the server-side facts about the transport are the only evidence the server itself contributes; security-guardian made the same observation at INFO
summary: A registry.write row names the agent (principal agent:<id>) and the command but not the session or the peer address that the other agent-originated audit rows carry; because the rows are asserted by the endpoint, the transport facts are the only evidence the server itself contributes. Deferred, together with the optional binding of the rows to the dispatch record: add the session id and peer address to the row's existing fields; the owner files it after the change is raised.

trigger: the plugin's dry-run option (a later change): a preview that wrote nothing is stored as registry.write success, or with another token as failure
classification_rationale: result maps ok to success and every other token to failure and never reads dry_run=; only free text in detail tells a preview apart, and the audit query has no detail filter by design; the grammar is owned by the plugin change
summary: result maps ok to success and every other token to failure and never reads dry_run=, so a preview that wrote nothing is stored as success (or as failure with another token) and only free text in detail tells it apart; the manual lists no dry-run outcome. Deferred to the change that adds the plugin's grammar: either dry runs emit no audit| line or the server maps an explicit token; recorded as a commitment, and the owner files it after the change is raised.

trigger: a recursive delete (a later change) emitting more than 300 audit lines in one 64 KB flush: the excess is dropped with a warning only
classification_rationale: E6 today because no producer emits audit| lines; architect noted I1 if lines drop, but the drop is now flagged and counted (reason=truncated) and the contract says a recursive delete is one record per operation, which the cap and the budget assume
summary: The 300-line cap ignores the agent's 64 KB output flush, so a recursive delete could exceed it and lose the excess with a warning only. The drop is now counted as reason=truncated, and the header contract says a recursive delete is one record per operation (the counts ride in fields). Deferred to the recursive-delete change: a cap derived from the flush size and a summary line; the owner files it after the change is raised.

trigger: the plugin change implements the producer side of the grammar: the pure half cannot be shared with the agent tests because plugin_result_audit.hpp includes audit_store.hpp (libpq), and no fuzz or property harness covers this parser of endpoint bytes
classification_rationale: architect (second half of its grammar finding) and quality-engineer raised the same gap; the existing fuzz harnesses cover the preflight and deployment parsers only
summary: The pure half of the audit| grammar cannot be shared with the agent's tests (its header includes the audit store and libpq) and no round-trip or fuzz harness covers the extractor, a parser of endpoint bytes. A seeded-random invariant test (at most 300 lines, at most 4,096 bytes, no control byte, audit| prefix) was added in 470e74049; the re-review found it never reached its bounds and it was strengthened (rab-seeded-bounds-test-is-vacuous). Deferred to the plugin change that owns the grammar: move the pure half to common/include/yuzu/ with a round-trip test; the owner files it after the change is raised.

trigger: a hostile enrolled agent, a hung audit table, a stop or kill part-way through a frame, a stream cut or a command that finishes after the gateway window compounds the recorded risks
classification_rationale: planning output only: six scenarios (two P0, three P1, one P2), none blocks the push and none derives above MEDIUM; nothing was run
summary: Six chaos scenarios were designed: a store failure mid-frame across a budget roll-over (CH-1), a fleet-wide answer under a hung audit table (CH-2), a stop or kill part-way through a gateway-forwarded 300-row frame (CH-3), replay and re-send fixtures at the hook (CH-4), a live stream cut, gateway kill and failover (CH-5), and the 300 s window boundary with delay, stagger and an operator retry (CH-6). A refusal followed by a store failure across a window roll-over is pinned by a unit case added in 577d75fe8 (close to the shape of CH-1); CH-2, CH-3, CH-5, CH-6 and the re-send fixtures of CH-4 are carried as a follow-up to re-run when a plugin first emits audit| lines, and the owner files it after the change is raised.

trigger: the registry plugin change makes the plugin emit audit| lines without settling these obligations: values are readable by every role holding AuditLog:Read or Response:Read for 365 days with no off switch
classification_rationale: commitments, not defects of this change: no producer emits audit| lines today (E6), the header banner's 'before a plugin emits' list carries them in code, and the gate is the emitting change's own review; enterprise-readiness listed them, architect (redaction can wait but must be settled) and compliance-officer (the producer contract has no duty to mask secret-class values) made the same point
summary: Obligations the emitting change owes, none of which is code in this change: publish the audit| grammar and the producer contract in the plugin README; decide how old= and new= render secret-class values; state the rollout order and the minimum agent version in upgrading.md (an agent without the stamp mints nothing, silently, and every server replica must be upgraded first); correct the audit-log wording 'per REQUEST rather than per device' once rows are per endpoint; make the gateway's command window cover delay and stagger (300 s plus both); keep the stamp on any new flush path. The first three are also listed in the header banner's 'before a plugin emits' list; the owner files the tracking issue after the change is raised.

trigger: two enrolled agents whose ids exceed 96 bytes and share their first 96 bytes (ids run to 256 bytes; an operator-set --agent-id; the default UUID is 36 bytes): one sends 600 or more audit rows in a window and the other's genuine rows are refused
classification_rationale: the documents said 'each agent' but DenialAuditBudget truncates every key to kAuditMaxKeyBytes (96, sized for the gateway guard's keys) while agent ids run to 256 bytes (auth::kMaxAgentIdLength), so the budget aliased agents; security-guardian derived HIGH (I1, MEDIUM natively, the missing audit event) and consistency-auditor derived HIGH (I2 and I1, medium natively); each probed the real header, and architect noted it as an INFO coupling note; the derived band governs
summary: The per-agent budget keyed on the first 96 bytes of the agent id, so two valid ids sharing their first 96 bytes shared one 600-row allowance and a looping agent could drain a neighbour's evidence; the shape is reachable because the Register charset admits 97 to 256 byte ids. Two reviewers reproduced it with probes over the real header and a third noted it. Fixed in 577d75fe8 at the root: DenialAuditBudget takes a trailing, defaulted max_key_bytes (the gateway guard keeps 96), the registry budget passes 256 with a static_assert against auth::kMaxAgentIdLength, and tests show that two 100-byte ids and two 256-byte ids differing only in their last byte are budgeted independently at the production configuration.

trigger: one fleet-wide registry.set_value (a Mutating pair, so broadcast is allowed) answered by more than 262,744 distinct agents inside one 60-second window on one server process; the dispatching replica ingests every gateway-connected agent's response
classification_rationale: measured twice with the real header at one row per agent in one window: 262,144 agents refuse 0, 300,000 refuse 37,256 (12.4%), 500,000 refuse 237,256 (47.5%); every agent past the table shared ONE 600-row allowance, first come first served, so the constant's comment ('sized for a fleet-wide change answered inside one window') was false at the declared scale (more than 1M agents; a design target of at least 500,000). Behaviour verified, reachability likely. happy-path derived HIGH (I1, I2; medium natively); enterprise-readiness derived MEDIUM (I7, same cause, SHOULD natively). The mitigating facts (the loss is counted, the raw output stays in the response store for 90 days, no plugin emits yet, the supported single-server size is 10,000 agents) are recorded and not used to cap the band
summary: The budget's agent table is exact for 262,144 agents per 60-second window, and every later agent shared one 600-row allowance, so a fleet-wide change answered by more agents than that lost rows (12.4% at 300,000 agents and 47.5% at 500,000, measured with the real header), below the documented design scale. Fixed in 577d75fe8: agents past the table are charged to one of 65,536 shared allowances chosen by a hash of the id, through the overflow key the budget already accepts, so 302,144 agents at one row each lose none. A looping agent in that region can exhaust the allowance it shares with about N/65,536 others, which is disclosed, and the documents now say the budget is per server process and a fixed window.

trigger: std::bad_alloc in the pure verdict (up to 300 events, about 1.3 MB) or in a catch arm, or a throw at row i after the budget refused earlier rows of the same frame
classification_rationale: the comment promised that anything the hook raises is reported as a failed write, but the try opened after the verdict and the store lock, and `refused` was declared inside the try so both catch arms lost it; cpp-safety and consistency-auditor derived MEDIUM, the others LOW or INFO, the strongest is recorded. Only an allocation failure can escape, and process_gateway_response already copies whole outputs unguarded, so the out-of-memory posture around the hook is unchanged
summary: The first firewall was narrower than its comment: the try opened after the pure verdict and the store lock, and the rows already refused by the budget were declared inside it, so a throw after a refusal booked neither suppressed nor persist_failed. Found by five reviewers. Fixed in 577d75fe8 in the code, not the comment: the try is the first statement, the owed count, the cursor and the refused count live outside it, and one lambda books suppressed and persist_failed on every exit including both catch arms; the comment now says exactly what is covered and that an allocation failure while reporting is not.

trigger: an edit deletes the try/catch, flips a 'return false' or drops the persist_failed booking: no test throws inside the hook, so every such edit stays green
classification_rationale: I5 if regressed (an uncaught throw from a detached forwarder terminates the process), I9 today; the closure of the earlier no-firewall finding rested on inspection; a seam exists (set_registry_audit_budget with a clock that throws, probed)
summary: No test threw inside the hook, so deleting the try/catch, flipping a return or dropping the persist_failed booking survived every suite, and the closure of the earlier no-firewall finding rested on inspection. Fixed in 577d75fe8 through the existing set_registry_audit_budget seam with a clock that throws: a std::exception and a non-std throw each give a false return, the error line and the gateway error line, persist_failed equal to the rows lost and suppressed equal to the rows refused first; a further case writes one row, refuses one and loses two across a window roll-over, which pins the three-way split of a frame's rows.

trigger: a later edit reverts the hook to the raw audit_store_ pointer, deletes the single set_registry_audit_store(audit_store_) line in server.cpp, or swaps the budget's two size_t constructor arguments: each leaves every test green
classification_rationale: the weak-store test was green on the pre-fix raw-pointer hook (both harnesses wired the raw pointer too and the reset test nulled it first), nothing read server.cpp, and no test sent more than 301 rows under the default budget. The false-green policy floor was considered by quality-engineer, security-guardian and architect and not applied: the reset test is not offered as closure evidence for the lifetime finding, whose closure is structural (shared owner, weak holder, per-frame lock behind the pure verdict, write-once) and is what the new gate pins
summary: Three closure mechanisms had no observing test or gate. The weak-store test passed against the pre-fix raw-pointer hook; nothing read server.cpp, so deleting the one set_registry_audit_store line turned every row off silently; and nothing pinned the production budget numbers, so swapped constructor arguments passed. Fixed in 577d75fe8 and 638025f01: neither harness wires the raw pointer any more, so a hook that reads it writes no row and the positive cases fail. The lexical gate now pins that the hook reads the store only through registry_audit_store_.lock(), that server.cpp wires the setter exactly once and never clears it, that the overflow key is computed once and charged on every row, and that the constructor calls make_registry_audit_budget, each with an in-file mutation. The production numbers are built by that one factory, static_asserts tie the budget to the frame cap and the overflow-bucket count to the table size, and pure cases pin 600 rows then refused and 302,144 agents at one row each losing none.

trigger: a regression in the exact-id predicate: 32-wide tails skip the hex check, only the last 8 characters are checked, / : ` or g is accepted, or the plugin-name test is removed
classification_rationale: a 120-mutant probe of the pure header left 31 survivors, six of them in this predicate; every bad-character row was 16 wide and all 'z'; quality-engineer labelled it SHOULD and derived LOW (they disagree, the derived band governs; neither gates)
summary: A 120-mutant probe of the pure header left 31 survivors, six of them in the exact-id predicate: 32-wide tails skipped the hex check, only the last eight characters or not the first were checked, / : backtick and g were accepted, and the plugin-name test could be removed. Fixed in 577d75fe8: a bad character first, middle and last at both widths, the neighbours of the three hex ranges, and an id with a one-byte-off plugin name (registrz-0123456789abcdef).

trigger: every run of the seeded random test (fixed seed): uniform random bytes put an LF about every 256 bytes, so frames hold at most 10 lines with a longest line of 1,810 bytes and no cut
classification_rationale: the 300-line and 4,096-byte assertions passed vacuously, while the cap and the cut are pinned elsewhere by literal sections and a live case, so this is test strength only; the generator is identical on every platform (mt19937 is fully specified)
summary: The seeded random bounds test never reached the bounds it asserts: 200 frames, at most 10 lines each, a longest line of 1,810 bytes and no cut frame, so only the control-byte scrub and the audit| prefix were exercised; other survivors were the auditx| prefix, the non-UTF-8 branch (checked for size only) and log_token versus log_id_token in the row. Fixed in 577d75fe8: the alphabet is skewed and many-short-lines frames are added, and the test requires that the run produced a cut line and a truncated frame so it cannot go vacuous again; the other survivors have cases, and the budget case stops the log capture before reading it.

caused_by: 470e74049 (the id helper written with the hex-id tests)
trigger: none: a convention breach (a printf-family call in new test code)
classification_rationale: docs/cpp-conventions.md lists printf-family calls under 'Forbidden in new code'; rejectable in one line (the same idiom exists in test_deployment_routes.cpp and is correct on all three compilers, and 30 unit-test files already use std::format), but adopted
summary: std::snprintf in the test id helper is a printf-family call that docs/cpp-conventions.md forbids in new code. Fixed in 577d75fe8: the helper uses std::format.

trigger: a producer author implements 'escapes the pipe' as a backslash: result parsing is not escape-aware, so a verbatim copy of the parser on a\|result=ok|result=refused returns ok
classification_rationale: the clause 'no |' is right, the rationale word 'escapes' is not; a percent-encoded pipe returns refused; band LOW (dormant producer) per docs-writer, with security-guardian to size; no producer exists
summary: The producer contract said the producer 'escapes' |, LF and CR so text cannot pick the row's result, but a backslash-escaped pipe still can (a verbatim copy of the result parser returns ok for a\|result=ok|result=refused) while a percent-encoded one does not. Fixed in 577d75fe8: the header and the audit-log row say the separators are replaced or percent-encoded so that no | byte remains.

trigger: an auditor follows the audit-log row's join list for a compliance remediation, a workflow step or a result-set producer
classification_rationale: the row's 'a dispatch the server makes itself (a compliance remediation)' contradicts the policy.remediate row (always operator-initiated; it records the execution id, not the command id), and the join list omitted two surfaces that do mint rows; docs-writer derived INFO, happy-path LOW
summary: The audit-log row called a compliance remediation 'a dispatch the server makes itself', contradicting the policy.remediate row (always operator-initiated; it records the execution id, not the command id), and omitted two surfaces that do mint rows: workflow steps (workflow.execute, detail execution_id only) and result-set producers (result_set.create, detail execution_id only). Fixed in 577d75fe8: the row says a compliance remediation's policy.remediate row carries the execution id, that workflow steps and result-set producers record only an execution id, and that this row's target_id is the join key.

trigger: an operator reads a zero counter as 'no loss', or a row is lost where the counter cannot see it: a frame after the audit store is reset, a stream that drops, the gateway's 300 s window, a throw after refused rows
classification_rationale: metrics.md ('This counter is complete'), the conventions bullet and the changelog ('everything not recorded is counted') contradicted the audit-log row's own list of uncounted losses; unhappy-path noted that a literal I2 or I7 reading of the silent drop would derive HIGH and treated it as the accepted, test-pinned stream-drop loss class, asking for adjudication if the ruling disagreed; the ruling agrees, so LOW stands
summary: metrics.md, the conventions bullet and the changelog called the counter complete ('everything not recorded is counted'), but a frame after the audit store is reset, a stream that drops and the gateway's 300 s window are uncountable by construction, 'moves emit_failed_total' held only for a store failure, and a throw after refused rows lost their tally. Fixed in 577d75fe8: the counter is described as complete for frames received while the audit store was up, the uncountable losses are listed, and the documents say not to sum across reason because two reasons count rows and two count frames.

trigger: an operator, auditor or on-call reads '600 rows per agent per 60 seconds' as a fleet property: the budget is an in-process member of each server replica, a fixed window (up to twice the rows across a boundary), reset by a restart, and first come first served inside an allowance
classification_rationale: security-guardian, compliance-officer, sre, docs-writer and enterprise-readiness each labelled this NICE, LOW or INFO; I7 on a required document derives MEDIUM, so the stronger band is recorded. compliance-officer also showed by probe that overflow is first-come truncation, not 'sampling' (20 agents x 100 rows beyond 4 tracked keys recorded 600 and refused 1,400)
summary: The documents said 'per agent' without 'per server process': the budget is in memory on each replica, so active-active replicas multiply it and a restart resets it. It is a fixed 60-second window, so a boundary can admit twice the rows; first-come truncation was called 'sampling'; and the window log line is count-only and names no agent, so there was no documented way to find a looping agent. Fixed in 577d75fe8: the audit-log row, the SOC 2 row, metrics.md, the conventions bullet and the changelog say per server process, fixed window and first come first served in an allowance, describe the window line as count-only, and say to find a looping agent by counting persisted registry.write rows per principal.

trigger: a reader of the release note takes 'dormant ... no rows are written and nothing else changes' at face value
classification_rationale: the audit-log row and the SOC 2 row state the server side is live on deploy and records any enrolled agent's lines, so nothing is concealed, but the changelog entry says otherwise; compliance-officer, docs-writer and enterprise-readiness labelled the gap LOW or NICE; I7 derives MEDIUM, so the stronger band is recorded
summary: The changelog entry ended 'so no rows are written and nothing else changes', which omits that the rows are asserted by the endpoint (the server checks the id shape and the stamped action, not a dispatch record) and that the server side is live on deploy; the audit-log and SOC 2 rows already said so. Fixed in 577d75fe8: the entry says the server side is live on deploy, no shipped agent or plugin writes rows, and the server records the lines of any enrolled agent up to the budget.

caused_by: 470e74049 (the comments and documents written for the first fix)
trigger: a reader of the comments and documents the first fix wrote
classification_rationale: comments that contradict the code are truth findings owned by the domain agent; the others are ordering and wording; the architect and gateway-erlang items are INFO and NICE and were adopted rather than rejected
summary: Wording and truth nits in the first fix's text, all adopted. 'Cut on a character boundary' is UTF-8 only (other bytes are cut at the bound); an Erlang test comment said __guard__ frames never reach handle_stream_response (true only of unsolicited ones); metrics.md split the retention counters around the new one; and the registry.write cell was not ordered for a reader. Stale 'Subscribe pair' wording in tests/meson.build and the lexical gate, a banner citing the wrong source for the final frame's action, and a server.cpp paragraph saying the store 'joined' a set it is not in were corrected. The header gained the sentence that a recursive delete is one record per operation, bounded_audit_budget.hpp now names its second consumer, and the shutdown comment says the gap is small in practice, not zero. All fixed in 577d75fe8.

trigger: a later edit renumbers action in gateway/priv/proto/** and regenerates: encode and decode are one module, so the test still passes (verified with a scratch mirror where action = 18)
classification_rationale: what the gap would admit is I1 for gateway-connected agents' rows, but E6 holds today (both proto mirrors, the canonical proto and the generated field number all say 8); no gate compares the vendored proto with the canonical one
summary: The management_pb round-trip test encoded and decoded in one module, so it pinned the key action, not wire field 8; regenerating management_pb from a mirror with action renumbered to 18 stayed green, and no gate compares the vendored proto with the canonical one. Fixed in 577d75fe8 with an assertion that the encoded bytes contain the field-8 tag, length and value (binary:match on <<66, 9, 'set_value'>>), verified green on the real codec and red on the renumbered mirror.

trigger: a typo in one of the four counter reason literals at an emit site
classification_rationale: rejected: the precedent (kRegisterInvalidAgentIdReasons) is a convenience, not a requirement, and the unit tests assert each of the four literals' counter after a real emit, so a typo at an emit site fails a test; derived INFO, so no independent adjudication is required
summary: The four counter reason strings are spelled at each emit site and at the server.cpp pre-seed rather than from one shared constexpr array, as the register-invalid-agent-id counter has. Not adopted: the array is a convenience, and the tests assert each literal's counter after a real emit, so a typo at an emit site fails a test.

trigger: one enrolled agent (compromised, or a faulty future plugin) sends a forged registry-<16 hex> id, a stamped set_value and 300 lines of 4,096 bytes continuously; nobody is paged on sustained suppressed, on any unmintable_id or on truncated
classification_rationale: growth is finite per principal and counted, so the I5 raise for unbounded growth no longer fires (compliance-officer derived MEDIUM; sre derived LOW for the missing alert). The arithmetic is compliance-officer's: 864,000 rows a day per hostile agent (1,440 windows x 600), about 4.3 KB a row, 3.7 to 4.1 GB a day into 365-day retention, no per-process ceiling, and the 16-connection pool every store shares saturates at about 800 flooding agents at 2 ms an insert. The rate of 600 per 60 seconds is kept: a legitimate agent writes about one row a command (a recursive delete is one record), and a scripted import of 100 to 150 values to one endpoint in a minute is the case a lower number would break; a byte-weighted budget and an unmintable_id alert (no legitimate source) want fleet data for their thresholds, sibling dropped-total families alert while the response-facet counters state that no alert ships, and the plugin is dormant
summary: The budget bounds rows per agent, not their cost: one hostile agent can write about 864,000 rows (3.7 to 4.1 GB) a day into 365-day retention, there is no per-process ceiling across agents, and no alert rule covers sustained suppressed, any unmintable_id or truncated (only persist_failed rides the existing YuzuAuditPersistFailures alert). The numbers are disclosed in the change description, and the conventions bullet states deliberately that no alert ships yet. Deferred: a byte-weighted budget (or a lower row budget) and alert rules with promtool cases, to land with or before the plugin release that first emits audit| lines; the owner files it after the change is raised.

trigger: store->log returns false and the next statement allocates (bad_alloc), or the second metric call inside a booking throws after the first succeeded
classification_rationale: the lambda that books a frame's refused and lost rows could run twice on one frame (once on the failed-store branch, again from a catch arm), over-counting suppressed or persist_failed once by at most 300 rows; the hook still returned false and logged. cpp-safety injected one bad_alloc at every allocating call of the verbatim hook body: 0 anomalies after the change, 7 before; unhappy-path found the same with a throwing counter. No unit test: the real binary cannot be made to fail an allocation (the mutant that removes the zeroing survives, recorded)
summary: book_rows was not idempotent: a throw after a booking was booked again from a catch arm. Fixed in 7a87c09a5: it zeroes what it booked (refused, and owed set to done), and the failed-store branch reads its not-attempted count before booking.

trigger: an allocation failure inside the pure verdict or the store lock, before the owed row count is known
classification_rationale: the hook comment said every owed row ends up written, refused or lost 'including when something throws', and the documents' list of uncounted losses omitted the case; a throw before the count is known loses up to 300 rows with only the error line and a false return. Booking one persist_failed for an unknown count was rejected (rows and frames would mix in one series)
summary: A throw before the verdict is taken counts nothing, against the comment and the loss list. Fixed in 7a87c09a5 in the words: the comment says 'once the verdict is taken' and that only the error line reports a failure inside the verdict, and audit-log.md and metrics.md list the case among the uncounted losses.

trigger: an exception in the hook's verdict, budget or store call (allocation failure)
classification_rationale: the documents said persist_failed also moves the alerted yuzu_server_audit_emit_failed_total; only AuditStore::log moves it, so the hook's catch arms book persist_failed without it and an exception-class failure never reaches the YuzuAuditPersistFailures alert
summary: The 'also moves the alerted counter' sentence held only when the store returns false. Fixed in 7a87c09a5 in four documents: 'a row the store itself fails to write also moves ...' (metrics.md, the observability conventions) and 'a failed store write' (audit-log.md, the changelog fragment).

trigger: selecting either case by name (the CI single-case retry)
classification_rationale: a comma in a Catch2 test name splits the by-name filter and matches no test (the binary prints 'No tests ran'), which defeats scripts/ci/flake-retry.py; tests/known-flaky.json is empty, so there was no live effect. Both names were introduced by the round-1 fix; a scan of every TEST_CASE in the file finds no other
summary: Two new test names contained commas. Fixed in 7a87c09a5 (both renamed); the mutation harness now also scans for the pattern.

trigger: a later edit of kRegistryAuditOverflowBuckets to between about 70 and 1,500
classification_rationale: the 302,144-agent case passes with fewer allowances (it stays green down to about 100 buckets, and 256 buckets lose 84,256 rows at 500,000 agents), so a later 'tuning' of the constant would bring the sampling cliff back with every test green. The shipped 65,536 is measured safe (0 refused up to 1.2M agents)
summary: The overflow allowance count was not tied to the fleet size the documents promise. Fixed in 7a87c09a5: a design-fleet constant (1.2M, the ADR-0006 scale) and a static_assert that the mean overflow load stays under a tenth of an allowance; audit-log.md now says where loss can start at that size (about twenty rows per agent in one window).

trigger: a later edit of a constant the documents quote, or of the hook's overflow argument (dropping it refuses 47.5% of rows at 500,000 agents)
classification_rationale: 262,144 and 65,536 were only symbolic in the tests (600, 60 s and 256 were literal), and the hook's overflow argument was seen only by the lexical pin: the budget cases build the key themselves and the hook cases inject small tables with fewer agents than keys; a second charge without the key passed the pin
summary: Two production facts had no runtime observer. Fixed in 7a87c09a5: literal checks of 262,144 and 65,536, and a live case that drives 16 agents through an 8-key budget and must write 16 rows, which only the hook's own overflow key achieves (11 without it).

trigger: a future edit: a raw store read the gate cannot see, a log string or block comment naming the raw store, a re-wrapped call
classification_rationale: the gate counted statements once per file or body, read string literals as code, did not check where the try opens, did not cover process_gateway_response, and had no benign controls (the sibling gate has them); two in-file mutations tripped two clauses each so a weakened clause stayed green. Not adopted: counting the setter across every server .cpp and a wiring-order pin (exotic; the gate's hint says to update it for a legitimate restructure)
summary: The lexical gate had bypasses and false-red surface. Fixed in 7a87c09a5: it pins the whole `const auto store = registry_audit_store_.lock();` statement, applies the raw-store rule to process_gateway_response, strips string literals first, requires the try to open before the verdict, and gains isolating mutations and four benign edits that must not be flagged; the docstring says what is pinned.

trigger: a reader of the SOC 2 readiness row
classification_rationale: the SOC 2 row listed two uncounted losses (a dropped stream, the gateway's 300-second window) where audit-log.md and metrics.md list three (plus frames after the store is released at shutdown)
summary: The SOC 2 row listed two of three uncounted losses. Fixed in 7a87c09a5 (the third added; the same edit changes 'no rows are written today' to 'no shipped agent or plugin writes any', which sat beside 'any enrolled agent is recorded').

trigger: a maintainer reading the hook comment or the shared primitive's header
classification_rationale: 'The metric is the complete signal' (hook) and 'the unsampled metric stays the complete count' (the shared header, written for the gateway guard and now sitting over a consumer whose refused row is a lost record) contradict the loss list the documents carry
summary: Two comments still called the counter complete. Fixed in 7a87c09a5: 'counts what the server sees go unrecorded' and 'the caller keeps an unsampled counter of refusals'.

trigger: a reader of the Signals paragraph of the registry.write row
classification_rationale: the reorder of the row dropped 'mutating': the verdict flags an unmintable id only for a registry MUTATING frame, never a read action's
summary: The Signals paragraph said unmintable_id counted any frame naming the plugin. Fixed in 7a87c09a5 ('registry mutating frames whose command_id ...').

trigger: a reader of the reordered registry.write row, the lexical gate's docstring, a test title
classification_rationale: 'cut' was used before it was defined; 'a boundary can admit up to twice that' needed 'a burst straddling a window boundary'; the gate docstring said 'sampling cliff' and 'no unit test reaches the hook's call' and its self-test sentence omitted the new mutations; a section title said 96 and 255 bytes where the ids share 99 and 255; '(the CHECK below)' named both a SQL constraint and a Catch2 macro; a static_assert message stated the primitive's rule instead of the requirement; the principal_role field row omitted agent
summary: Reader-order and small wording defects in what the round-1 fix wrote. All fixed in 7a87c09a5.

trigger: an actor able to enrol more than 262,144 agents in one window (an unlimited enrollment token or an auto-approve policy) who also chooses ids that hash into a victim's overflow allowance
classification_rationale: std::hash is unseeded and a colliding id took about 32,000 tries; the effect is that window's evidence for the colliding agent, counted as suppressed and not attributable. A per-process salt buys nothing: an actor able to enrol 262,144 ids already covers every one of the 65,536 allowances. The header says the hash is not a defence against a chosen id and the operator documents say the looping agent 'exhausts the allowance it shares'
summary: A chosen agent id can be made to collide with a victim's in the overflow region, at a scale that needs more than 262,144 live enrolled ids. Rejected as an accepted trade-off with the evidence above; no change.

policy_floor: ownership/lifetime defect enumerated by cpp-safety's blocking contract (borrowed-data escape: a detached, unjoined thread leasing a pool its owner is destroying)
trigger: server stop() (SIGTERM) while a gateway-forwarded registry mutating frame with audit| lines is between two rows of the hook on a detached forwarder thread: pg_pool_.reset() completes and the thread's next store->log() leases a destroyed pool
classification_rationale: the weak-store handoff keeps the AuditStore OBJECT alive but nothing registers the hook with the pool it borrows: ~PgPool waits only for leases and waiters it can see, and a forwarder between two rows is neither; the hook comment, the stop() comment and the architect's INFO row all priced the reach as one lease, not a per-row loop of up to 300 synchronous writes; derived MEDIUM (I5, E5), gated by the lifetime policy floor; nobody forced the race (reviewed by reading, Codex confirmed the path, no dynamic reproduction)
summary: A forwarder that has locked the weak store holds it across up to 300 synchronous store->log() calls, each of which leases the borrowed pg::PgPool&. ServerImpl::stop() resets audit_store_ and then pg_pool_ with nothing between them that waits, and the forwarder threads are never joined (#3279), so a forwarder BETWEEN two rows is invisible to ~PgPool and its next row leases a destroyed pool. Fixed in 5bc2f07c6: the hook runs inside a RundownGate (entered after the pure verdict and before the weak lock, checked before every row); stop() closes it and waits up to 15 s for the hooks inside before it resets the store and the pool, and exits the process on timeout. Rows lost to the close are counted as persist_failed; a frame after it records nothing. The reviewer's second effect (a late ~AuditStore join) does not occur: stop() joins the retention thread at server.cpp:10396, before the reset.

The new audit hook dereferenced the raw audit_store_ pointer on the detached forwarder threads that shutdown does not drain, while stop() nulls and frees the store: a use-after-free window the base code did not have, found independently by five reviewers and gated by the lifetime policy floor. Fixed in 470e74049 the way the analytics store was treated: the server owns the store as a shared_ptr, the service holds a weak_ptr written once at wiring and never cleared, the pure verdict runs first, and the store is locked per frame only when the frame owes rows or a flag. The re-review confirmed the hook no longer reads the raw pointer (ASan, UBSan and TSan probes). CORRECTION (pr-review fjarvis, df3bfc291): the pool the store borrows was NOT unchanged by that fix, as this row first said: the strong reference spans up to 300 synchronous writes that each lease the pool, so a forwarder between two rows could lease a pool stop() was destroying. That is rab-pool-reach-held-across-the-row-loop-at-shutdown, closed by the rundown gate in 5bc2f07c6. The detached thread itself is the pre-existing #3279 gap, unchanged. The first test evidence for the closure was weak (rab-closure-mechanisms-have-no-observing-test-or-gate).
